ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Circles $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, and $\omega_3$ each have radius $4$ and are placed in the plane so that each circle is externally tangent to the other two. Points $P_1$, $P_2$, and $P_3$ lie on $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, and $\omega_3$ respectively such that $P_1P_2=P_2P_3=P_3P_1$ and line $P_iP_{i+1}$ is tangent to $\omega_i$ for each $i=1,2,3$, where $P_4 = P_1$. See the figure below. The area of $\triangle P_1P_2P_3$ can be written in the form $\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}$ for positive integers $a$ and $b$. What is $a+b$?

Point P1 is on the lower right side of the upper circle ω1, point P2 is on the lower-right circle ω2, and point P3 is on the lower-left circle ω3. Each side of the triangle is tangent to the corresponding circle in cyclic order, and the circle centers are all located in the normal direction outside the gray triangle. Establish coordinates according to the specified method. Let the side length of the equilateral triangle be s, and take P1=(0,0), P2=(s,0), P3=(s/2,-√3s/2). Since P_iP_{i+1} is the tangent line of ω_i, the perpendicular distance from the corresponding circle center O_i to that side is the radius 4. According to the normal branch in which the circle centers in the figure are located outside the triangle, take O1=(0,-4). For side P2P3, the corresponding circle center is O2=(s-2√3,2). The radii of the three circles are all 4 and they are externally tangent pairwise, so O1O2=8. Thus (s-2√3)^2+(2-(-4))^2=8^2, that is, (s-2√3)^2+36=64, so (s-2√3)^2=28. Calculating gives s^2=(2√3+2√7)^2=40+8√21, therefore the area is (√3/4)(40+8√21)=10√3+6√7=√300+√252. So a=300, b=252, and a+b=552.

Let O_i be the circle centers and let G be the common center of the equilateral center triangle and the equilateral P-triangle for the depicted symmetric branch. Since O1O2=8, the circumradius of triangle O1O2O3 is GO_i=8/sqrt(3). Let x=GP_i, the circumradius of triangle P1P2P3. Because P_iP_{i+1} is tangent to omega_i at P_i, O_iP_i is perpendicular to side P_iP_{i+1}. In an equilateral triangle, the segment from a vertex to the center makes a 30-degree angle with each adjacent side, so in the branch shown angle GP_iO_i=60 degrees. In triangle G P_i O_i, use O_iP_i=4 and GO_i=8/sqrt(3): (8/sqrt(3))^2=x^2+4^2-2(x)(4)cos60, so x^2-4x-16/3=0 and x=2+2sqrt(7/3). 图像描述：图中有三个等半径圆，ω1 在上方，ω2 在右下方，ω3 在左下方，三圆两两外切。灰色三角形的三个顶点分别标为 P1、P2、P3，其中 P1 在 ω1 上，P2 在 ω2 上，P3 在 ω3 上。三角形的边分别贴着对应圆作切线，整体呈现 120 度旋转对称的形态。

推理：设三个圆心为 O1、O2、O3。因为三个半径都是 4 且两两外切，所以 O1O2=O2O3=O3O1=8，圆心三角形 O1O2O3 是边长 8 的等边三角形。设其中心为 G，则 GOi 是该等边三角形的外接圆半径，所以 GOi=8/sqrt(3)。

由图中的对称分支，等边三角形 P1P2P3 与圆心等边三角形共用中心 G。设 x=GPi，即三角形 P1P2P3 的外接圆半径。

因为 PiP(i+1) 与 ωi 在 Pi 处相切，所以 OiPi 垂直于边 PiP(i+1)。在等边三角形 P1P2P3 中，从顶点 Pi 到中心 G 的线与相邻边成 30 度角。因此在图示分支中，角 GPiOi=60 度。

在三角形 G-Pi-Oi 中，OiPi=4，GOi=8/sqrt(3)，GPi=x。由余弦定理：
(8/sqrt(3))^2 = x^2 + 4^2 - 2·x·4·cos60°。
所以 64/3 = x^2 + 16 - 4x，即 x^2 - 4x - 16/3 = 0。
解得正根 x = 2 + 2sqrt(7/3)。

等边三角形外接圆半径为 x 时，面积为 (3sqrt(3)/4)x^2。代入得面积 = 10sqrt(3)+6sqrt(7)。写成 sqrt(a)+sqrt(b) 的形式：10sqrt(3)=sqrt(300)，6sqrt(7)=sqrt(252)。因此 a+b=300+252=552。

由图中的对称分支，等边三角形 P1P2P3 与圆心等边三角形共用中心 G。设 x=GPi，即三角形 P1P2P3 的外接圆半径。

因为 PiP(i+1) 与 ωi 在 Pi 处相切，所以 OiPi 垂直于边 PiP(i+1)。在等边三角形 P1P2P3 中，从顶点 Pi 到中心 G 的线与相邻边成 30 度角。因此在图示分支中，角 GPiOi=60 度。

在三角形 G-Pi-Oi 中，OiPi=4，GOi=8/sqrt(3)，GPi=x。由余弦定理：
(8/sqrt(3))^2 = x^2 + 4^2 - 2·x·4·cos60°。
所以 64/3 = x^2 + 16 - 4x，即 x^2 - 4x - 16/3 = 0。
解得正根 x = 2 + 2sqrt(7/3)。

等边三角形外接圆半径为 x 时，面积为 (3sqrt(3)/4)x^2。代入得面积 = 10sqrt(3)+6sqrt(7)。写成 sqrt(a)+sqrt(b) 的形式：10sqrt(3)=sqrt(300)，6sqrt(7)=sqrt(252)。因此 a+b=300+252=552。

raw_record.original_question: Circles $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, and $\omega_3$ each have radius $4$ and are placed in the plane so that each circle is externally tangent to the other two. Points $P_1$, $P_2$, and $P_3$ lie on $\omega_1$, $\omega_2$, and $\omega_3$ respectively such that $P_1P_2=P_2P_3=P_3P_1$ and line $P_iP_{i+1}$ is tangent to $\omega_i$ for each $i=1,2,3$, where $P_4=P_1$. See the figure below. The area of $\triangle P_1P_2P_3$ can be written in the form $\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}$ for positive integers $a$ and $b$. What is $a+b$?
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: in the figure there are three circles with the same radius, labeled ω1, ω2, ω3, and the three circles are externally tangent pairwise; the gray region is the equilateral triangle P1P2P3. Point P1 is on the lower right side of the upper circle ω1, point P2 is on the lower-right circle ω2, and point P3 is on the lower-left circle ω3. Each side of the triangle is tangent to the corresponding circle in cyclic order, and the circle centers are all located in the normal direction outside the gray triangle.

Establish coordinates according to the specified method. Let the side length of the equilateral triangle be s, and take P1=(0,0), P2=(s,0), P3=(s/2,-√3s/2). Since P_iP_{i+1} is the tangent line of ω_i, the perpendicular distance from the corresponding circle center O_i to that side is the radius 4.

According to the normal branch in which the circle centers in the figure are located outside the triangle, take O1=(0,-4). For side P2P3, the corresponding circle center is O2=(s-2√3,2). The radii of the three circles are all 4 and they are externally tangent pairwise, so O1O2=8.

Thus (s-2√3)^2+(2-(-4))^2=8^2, that is, (s-2√3)^2+36=64, so (s-2√3)^2=28. From the larger positive side-length branch in the figure, s=2√3+2√7.

The area of the equilateral triangle is (√3/4)s^2. Calculating gives s^2=(2√3+2√7)^2=40+8√21, therefore the area is (√3/4)(40+8√21)=10√3+6√7=√300+√252. So a=300, b=252, and a+b=552.
